0.4.0.title: What's new in Meldmind
bullets: The app is now called Meldmind. It is still an Everborn product. Take command of all your AIs.
The top bar is grouped dropdown menus: Work, Create, Business, Connect, and Settings.
Council is on the order box: several AIs answer, review each other, and a chair writes the verdict.
Pro prompts are written by our team. Auto-detect can suggest one from what you type, and you can remove that chip.
Open live view sits at the bottom-right of Live Ops.
Connect an API key, or an MCP server, from the Connect menu.
Pipelines and scheduled agents are in the Work menu. A scheduled result that would be sent waits until you approve it.
Publishing shows a preview first. Nothing posts until you confirm.

0.4.3.title: What's new in Meldmind
bullets: Simple and Expert. A new install starts in Simple: one chat box, and the council picks the AI.
The first time you open Meldmind it asks: Keep it simple or show me everything?
A Simple / Expert switch sits in the top bar on every screen. One click changes it. Your chats, projects, and keys stay put.
Simple shows Chat, Projects, Create, and Settings. Expert keeps the debate, the scores, spend caps, the live map, marketplace, MCP, webhooks, and every menu.
The chips under the chat box list only AIs you have connected. Demo stays there only until a real AI is connected.
Pasting a key recognizes Gemini auth keys (AQ.) and older AIza keys, plus Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, OpenRouter, and Groq. Gemini is checked on Google's own models list.
Help is a tab in Simple and in Expert. Search the guides, or click Ask Meldmind. Take the tour again and Check for updates are both there.
Phone pairing uses this PC's Wi-Fi address when you turn it on in Settings, under Phone and other devices. The QR code and the link both include the pairing code. It stays off until you turn it on.
This note shows once after an update. Take the tour again any time from Settings.

0.4.2.title: What's new in Meldmind
bullets: Connect Google Drive, Instagram, HighLevel and Slack with your own sign-in, in Settings, Publishing. Every post, schedule or save shows a preview and waits for your click.
Services that offer both, such as Kling, can connect with an API key or an MCP server.
Marketplace: browse and install signed templates, or share one of your own pipelines.
Steadier app: clearer error messages, empty screens that say what to do next, keyboard and screen reader fixes, and a user guide.
